preview_text: Canada enter as favorites and co-hosts, playing in front of a home crowd with real expectations to advance from the group. Jesse Marsch has built a high-pressing 4-4-2 that excels in transition — Canada have conceded just 0.5 goals per game since the 2024 Copa America.

Jonathan David is the primary goal threat at $10,500 — Juventus striker with 33 goals in 84 international caps. His partnership with Buchanan and Davies on the flanks is the engine of the Canadian attack. Davies carries a Q tag; his availability is the most important lineup note for this game.

Ismael Kone carries a Q designation (Illness). If he misses, the Canadian midfield structure changes and minutes redistribute. Alphonso Davies (Q, Hamstring) is the bigger concern — Canada's attacking tempo is heavily tied to his role as an advanced left-sided threat.

Tajon Buchanan at $6,800 carries strong opto at 27.3% with confirmed wide role. Alistair Johnston at $4,200 projects well for a defender with set piece involvement and attacking full-back duties in Marsch's system.

Bosnia arrive having beaten both Wales and Italy via penalty shootouts in qualifying — Barbarez has built a resilient, well-organized side that conceded just 0.9 goals per game through European qualifying. They are not here to make up the numbers.

Esmir Bajraktarevic ($6,300) leads Bosnia's projection at 10.55 fpts and is a confirmed CK taker with 42.6% projected ownership. His American-born profile and Roma experience make him Bosnia's most DFS-relevant player. Edin Dzeko carries a Q tag — his availability as the focal striker significantly affects the BIH ceiling.

Dzeko (Q, Undisclosed) is the lynchpin of Bosnia's attack at 40 years old. Barbarez has been known to pair him with Demirovic or Tabakovic (OUT, Ankle) — with Tabakovic confirmed out, Demirovic ($5,700) at S1 is the backup plan if Dzeko misses.

Ivan Basic at $3,300 and Benjamin Tahirovic at $3,000 represent the floor of BIH salary — both project reasonably at tournament price. Bosnia committed the most fouls per game in European qualifying, suggesting set piece volume in both directions.

USA are co-hosts and slight favorites at 49.6% implied win probability. Pochettino's 3-4-2-1 deploys Pulisic and Tillman as inverted attacking midfielders with Robinson bombing forward from left wingback — that trio generates the primary attacking threat.

Christian Pulisic ($9,800) leads the slate at 13.66 projected fpts with 57.3% projected ownership and confirmed FK+CK duties. Antonee Robinson ($6,700) at 47.1% opto is the optimizer's pick — 11.90 fpts projection from a defensive position is elite value at that salary.

Chris Richards carries a Q tag (Ankle, 6/12). His replacement in the back three is worth monitoring at lineup release — the USA's 3-back structure means a change here affects how far Robinson and Dest push forward, which filters up to their DFS projections.

Weston McKennie ($4,500) and Sergino Dest ($4,800) both project around 8.5 fpts at salaries that allow stacking the top USA names. Folarin Balogun ($8,700) leads the line at 9.94 fpts with 22.3% ownership — lower chalk than expected for a starting striker.

Paraguay averaged just 38% possession in CONMEBOL qualifying — Alfaro's side sits deep, defends compactly, and looks to spring Almiron and Enciso on the counter. They conceded just 0.56 goals per game in qualifying, second only to Ecuador.

Miguel Almiron ($6,200) at 9.68 fpts is the Paraguay attack's most reliable source — Newcastle's all-time leading Premier League scorer brings proven quality at a reasonable salary. Julio Enciso carries a Q designation (Thigh) and his availability significantly impacts Paraguay's creative ceiling.

Damian Bobadilla is also Q (Knee, 6/12) for Paraguay. Both Bobadilla and Enciso GTD on the same slate creates meaningful uncertainty around the Paraguay midfield structure. Diego Gomez at $5,200 picks up additional set piece responsibilities if Enciso is unavailable.

Juan Jose Caceres ($4,400) projects at 7.92 fpts with 25.4% opto — high output for a right-back driven by set piece involvement and Paraguay's directness in attack. Antonio Sanabria ($5,900) is the secondary striker option with 14.6% opto at manageable salary.
